quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and can't find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note on the vehicle with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal and stay off the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before braking or turning.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on state highways is:

options.text: 55 mph.
65 mph.
75 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: State highways have a 55 mph speed limit. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: Streets and highways are most slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts because water mixes with oil and other chemicals on the road. Drive with extra caution during the first half hour of rain.

questions.question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the centerline on the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then continue looking ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route to your destination.
Proceed to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway. Continue to the next exit instead. Backing up surprises other drivers and causes accidents.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always sound your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A school crossing sign means you are near a school. Stay alert and be prepared to stop for children.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels toward the road edge when parking uphill without a curb. This keeps the car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching you.
Come to a full stop then proceed when it is safe to do so.
Proceed carefully through the intersection, not always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop then proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. Stop at the marked line or before the crosswalk. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.
Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Stay in the left lane completely when passing a motorcycle. Don't crowd the motorcycle's lane. Returning too soon can force the rider off the road.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates danger. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you too close, take your foot off the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without needing to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, add extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision with the tailgater.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire suddenly goes flat, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: An orange and red triangle on the back of a vehicle always means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display an orange and red triangle on the back. These include farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the roadway.
Toward the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road. This prevents blindness from their headlights and helps you stay on course. Do not retaliate by keeping your bright lights on.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat it like a stop sign.
Cannot proceed until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light the same as a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge from the right side.

questions.question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, you:

options.text: Must stay within your lane.
May cross the centerline to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic is moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use your high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles may not see you.
Vehicles behind you may drive too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect the light back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the car in park.
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the car in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave the car in park when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road so the car rolls to safety if brakes fail.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: This sign warns of:

options.text: A right turn.
An intersection.
A lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop or turn.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Speed up to match traffic speed, but only after you have found a safe gap. Wait for the gap to appear before speeding up.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance at the right edge of the road instead of looking at the bright lights. This keeps your car on the road safely.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. You should:

options.text: Make room if possible.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Stay in your lane no matter what.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room if possible.
questions.explanation: When safe, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: A car is following you too closely on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually so the other driver will pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between the cars.
Brake suddenly, then resume your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually so the other driver will pass you.
questions.explanation: If another driver is tailgating you, slow down gradually. This encourages them to pass you. If you can, move to a different lane. Never speed up or brake suddenly.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Reduce your speed, check traffic, and then gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Your car starts to skid out of control. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not touch the brakes. Steer to correct the skid until your car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: You are approaching a traffic light showing steady yellow. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light and have not yet entered the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: How far before turning should you activate your turn signal?

options.text: 20 feet
100 feet
200 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal 100 feet before you turn. This gives other drivers enough time to see your signal and prepare for your turn.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate. You find a gap, match the traffic speed, and signal. What should you do next?

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in because you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: After you identify a gap and match traffic speed, merge carefully when it is safe. Watch other traffic closely and do not expect drivers to move out of the way.

questions.question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: You are on the freeway following a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the truck driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Follow trucks at a greater distance than regular vehicles. If you are too close, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating removes your safety margin if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: You are about to be hit from behind. Which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting other vehicles.

questions.question: You are stopping on snow or ice in a car with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS). What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The ABS system will pump the brakes faster than you can.
